subject: math
examFormat: EJU Mathematics is a SEPARATE 80-minute booklet (not part of the Science booklet). Two courses are offered and the examinee takes exactly one: Course 1 (Basic, コース1) covers syllabus topics 1-7; Course 2 (Advanced, コース2) covers all topics 1-20 and is required by science/engineering faculties. This knowledge base targets Course 2. Each course paper has four large questions (大問 I, II, III, IV), each split into sub-questions (Q1, Q2, …) and parts (1),(2),(3). Answers are NOT multiple-choice: every blank is labelled by a letter (A, B, C, …) and is filled on a mark-sheet with a single numeral 0-9 OR a minus sign. Consecutive letters concatenate into a number, the numerator/denominator of a fraction, an exponent, etc. (e.g. b = -BC with B=2, C=4 means b = -24; a fraction L/M with L=1, M=3 means 1/3). Answer-letters reset at the start of each large question. Conventions: reduce square roots fully, put any minus sign on the numerator, and reduce fractions to lowest terms. A few sub-parts instead ask the examinee to pick the correct expression from a labelled list 0~9 (still entered as a single digit). Some answer letters are intentionally left blank.

questionArchetypes.description: Two quadratics are given with vertex / value conditions (e.g. g minimized at a given x, and g(k)=f(k)); determine the coefficients, find the non-trivial intersection by reducing to a quadratic, then maximize the difference f(x)-g(x) over the resulting interval. Pure symbolic + integer answers.
questionArchetypes.exampleStem: f(x)=-2x^2, g(x)=x^2+ax+b with g minimized at x=3 and g(4)=f(4); find a,b, the min of g, the other intersection x, and the max of f-g on [-2,4]. (2021_1 C2 I-Q1)

questionArchetypes.description: Two players each draw a card and compare; compute the single-trial probabilities of draw/win, then for n repeated independent trials compute binomial/multinomial probabilities (e.g. 'A wins >= 3 of 4') and use symmetry to get P(A>B) = (1 - P(tie))/2.
questionArchetypes.exampleStem: Each of A,B has cards 1,2,3; play four times; P(draw), P(A wins >=3), P(one win/one loss/two draws), P(equal wins), P(A>B). (2021_1 C2 I-Q2)

questionArchetypes.description: Regular tetrahedron of side 1; points P,Q divide two edges in ratio x:(1-x); express OP,OQ as position vectors (choose from a list), compute |OP|=|OQ| and OP.OQ as functions of x, then bound cos(angle POQ) over 0<x<1.
questionArchetypes.exampleStem: Regular tetrahedron OABC; find the range of cos(angle POQ): 1/2 < cos <= 5/6. (2021_1 C2 II-Q1)

questionArchetypes.description: Triangle on the complex plane with vertices A(α),B(β),C(γ) defined by a ratio (γ-α)/(β-α)=given complex number; convert to polar form, interpret as a rotation+scaling about A, find |w| and arg w for a related ratio, and derive side-length ratios under a constraint like α+β+γ=0.
questionArchetypes.exampleStem: (γ-α)/(β-α)=1-i; polar form √2(cos 7π/4 + i sin 7π/4); rotation by 7π/4 and scaling by √2. (2021_1 C2 II-Q2)

questionArchetypes.description: Minimize a symmetric exponential expression by substituting t = 2^x + 2^{-x} (so 4^x+4^{-x}=t^2-2, 8^x+8^{-x}=t^3-3t), reduce to a cubic g(t), restrict t>=2, and use g'(t) to locate local/global extrema; recover x via logs.
questionArchetypes.exampleStem: Minimize f(x)=8^x+8^{-x}-... using t=2^x+2^{-x}; find the minimum value and the x attaining it. (2021_1 C2 III)

questionArchetypes.description: Two curves (e.g. y=sin^2 x and y=k cos 2x on [0,π/2]) bound regions of area S1 and S2; set up the intersection, integrate, and prove S2-S1 is a constant independent of the parameter k.
questionArchetypes.exampleStem: C1: y=sin^2 x, C2: y=k cos 2x; show S2-S1 = π/4 independent of k. (2021_1 C2 IV)

questionArchetypes.description: Given the sum of the first n terms S_n as a quadratic in n, recover the term a_n, define a product sequence b_n = a_n * a_{n+k}, then find T_n = sum of b_n and its minimum by locating where the terms change sign.
questionArchetypes.exampleStem: S_n=(n^2-17n)/4, b_n=a_n*a_{n+5}; find T_n and its minimum. (2020_2 C2 II-Q1)

questionArchetypes.description: Put a complex number in polar form, solve z^n = (that number) for all roots in 0<=arg<2π, order them by argument, and relate the roots of a related higher-degree equation (e.g. w^8-16w^4+256=0) back to those roots; compute products like w_1 w_8.
questionArchetypes.exampleStem: 8+8√3 i in polar form; solve z^4=8+8√3 i; link to w^8-16w^4+256=0. (2020_2 C2 II-Q2)

questionArchetypes.description: Find the tangent to a cubic at a given point and the tangent drawn from an external point; locate their intersection C; then compute the angle θ between the two lines via tan α, tan β and the tangent-subtraction formula.
questionArchetypes.exampleStem: f(x)=x^3-4x+4; tangent at A(-1,7) and tangent from B(0,-12); find tan θ. (2020_2 C2 III)

questionArchetypes.description: For f(x)=Σ (sin kx)/k on [0,π], differentiate (f' is a quadratic in cos x) to find the critical points, prove f(x)>0 on (0,π), and integrate to get the area between the curve and the x-axis.
questionArchetypes.exampleStem: f(x)=sin x + (sin 2x)/2 + (sin 3x)/3; show f>0 on (0,π) and find the enclosed area. (2020_2 C2 IV)

styleNotes: Course 2 papers consist of four large questions (I-IV). A typical mix: I tends to combine an algebra/quadratics part with a counting/probability part; later questions range over the advanced topics — vectors (often a tetrahedron or plane-figure setup), the complex plane (rotation/similarity of triangles), calculus (min/max via a clever substitution; areas/volumes between curves; proving a quantity is independent of a parameter), sequences/recurrences, exponential-log, and trigonometry. Answers are exact integers, reduced fractions, or reduced surds, entered digit-by-digit into lettered boxes. Phrasing is terse and guided: the problem walks the student through intermediate boxed results that are reused later (shaded when reused). Generate new questions that follow this guided, multi-part, digit-fill structure and the same topic mixes; keep every answer an exact value that fits single-digit boxes after reduction.
ingestionNote: Taxonomy and format encoded from the 2026 syllabus and the 2021_1 Course 2 paper (answers verified by solving and against the official key). Per-paper Course 2 extractions are being added under past-questions/math/ as fully-verified RichExams. Answer format is digit-fill, not multiple-choice.
